title: Paul and Peter: Christ gave himself to rescue and make us live to him
source_text: IX. Nam ut testatur Paulus, Dominus noster Jesus Christus dedit semetipsum pro peccatis nostris, ut eriperet nos de praesenti saeculo nequam, Galat. 1. Et pro omnibus mortuus est Christus, ut qui vivunt jam non sibi vivant, sed ei qui pro ipsis mortuus est, & resurrexit, 2 Cor. 5. Quibus concinit illud Petri, Peccata nostra ipse pertulit in corpore suo super lignum, ut peccato mortui justitiae vivamus. 1 Pet. 2. Denique, juxta Apostolum, huc tendit illa gratia salutaris, quae in Evangelio nobis apparuit, ut abnegantes impietatem, & saecularia desideria, sobrie, pie, & juste vivamus in hoc saeculo. Tit. 2.
pass_a_gloss: For as Paul testifies, our Lord Jesus Christ gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from the present evil age (Galatians 1). And Christ died for all, that those who live may no longer live for themselves, but for him who died for them and rose again (2 Corinthians 5). With which agrees that of Peter: He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we, dead to sin, might live to righteousness (1 Peter 2). Finally, according to the Apostle, that saving grace which appeared to us in the Gospel tends to this, that denying ungodliness and worldly desires, we may live soberly, piously, and justly in this age (Titus 2).
pass_b_english: Christ gave himself to rescue us from this evil age and make the living live for him (Galatians 1; 2 Corinthians 5).
Peter and Titus tie his bearing of sins to dead-to-sin, sober, pious, just life.

lemmas.gloss: dead to sin we may live to righteousness
